import re

# Negated class: one character that is not in the menu.
print(re.findall(r"[^aeiou ]", "lexer rules"))           # every consonant
print(re.fullmatch(r"#[^\n]*", "# note\nx = 1"))          # None: the class cannot cross the newline
print(re.match(r"#[^\n]*", "# note\nx = 1").group())      # the comment stops at the newline

# A class excludes characters, not a sequence.
by_class     = r"/\*[^*/]*\*/"
by_lookahead = r"/\*(?:(?!\*/).)*\*/"
for c in ["/* plain */", "/* a * b */", "/* x / y */", "/* one */ two */"]:
    print(f"{c!r:20} class={bool(re.fullmatch(by_class, c))!s:5} lookahead={bool(re.fullmatch(by_lookahead, c))}")

# A whole line with no TODO anywhere in it.  Case matters.
for line in ["x = 1", "# TODO: fix", "y = 2  # todo later"]:
    print(f"{line!r:22} {bool(re.fullmatch(r'(?!.*TODO).*', line))}")
description: You can compare a negated character class with a negative lookahead that checks a whole sequence.

steps.description: The first class selects consonants. The comment pattern stops at a newline, so match can return the comment while fullmatch rejects the whole input.
by_class excludes each star and slash from the body. by_lookahead checks for the closing pair before consuming each character.

steps.answer: The lookahead pattern accepts it. The class pattern excludes that star.
steps.question: Which pattern accepts the comment containing a lone star?

steps.description: The loop compares both patterns with fullmatch. Both reject the input with text after the first closing pair.
The final lookahead checks for uppercase TODO anywhere in the line. The lowercase todo passes because case matters.
The displayed results distinguish excluding individual characters from excluding a substring. The TODO check rejects the uppercase occurrence and accepts the lowercase one.
